description: Somos Fénix Orbital, estudiantes del Tecnológico de Zacatepec. Nos interesa convertir los residuos que rodean la Luna y Marte en recursos útiles para futuras misiones espaciales. Aportamos investigación, gestión de proyectos, redacción, diseño y presentación de ideas, con muchas ganas de aprender. Si te apasiona el espacio y quieres crear soluciones reales, ¡únete a nosotros! Buscamos compañeros curiosos, responsables y comprometidos, con ideas nuevas y gusto por aprender y crecer en equipo.
summary: We developed Beyond the Mission, a narrative video pitch that tells the story of an object abandoned in space, from its own point of view. After completing its mission, it is left forgotten in the orbits of the Moon and Mars, drifting aimlessly alongside other debris humanity has left behind. To address the challenge, we used storytelling. Instead of showing only technical data, we give a voice to an object that was once useful and is now space debris. This makes the problem relatable, emotional and easy for any audience to understand. The project matters because exploration of the Moon and Mars is growing quickly, and so is the amount of debris left in their orbits. This debris can put future missions at risk and threaten the sustainability of space. Our goal is to raise awareness so people understand that space is not an endless dumping ground for what we no longer need, and that every mission should consider what it leaves behind.
details:
What does it do / how does it work?
Beyond the Mission is a narrative video told from the point of view of an abandoned space object. Viewers follow it from its launch, when it was useful and had a purpose, until its mission ends and it is left forgotten in the orbits of the Moon and Mars, surrounded by other debris. Through its story, the video shows how space debris builds up and why it is a real problem.

What are its benefits?
It explains a technical topic in a simple, visual and emotional way, so anyone can understand it without prior knowledge. It is easy to share on social media, in schools and at outreach events, so it can reach a wide audience.

What is the intended impact?
We want to raise awareness about the debris we leave in space, especially as missions to the Moon and Mars increase. We hope viewers, especially young people, will think about each mission’s responsibility for what it leaves behind and see space sustainability as everyone’s concern.

What tools did you use?
We used NASA resources and tools. We consulted official information on NASA’s website about space debris and missions to the Moon and Mars, and used it to give the story a real scientific basis. We also used NASA images and visual materials to accurately portray the space environment. We edited the video in CapCut, where we combined scenes, narration, music and effects. We also used Claude, an artificial intelligence tool, to help organize ideas and draft written content for the project.

How is the project creative?
Instead of presenting data and charts, we give a voice and personality to an inanimate object. Telling the story in the first person makes viewers empathize with something they would normally see as junk, which makes the message memorable.

What factors did the team consider?

  • Making the message clear for people of all ages.
  • Basing the story on real information about debris in lunar and Martian orbits.
  • Keeping the video short enough to hold attention.
  • Using royalty-free or properly licensed images and music.
  • Drawing on the skills of all five team members, who come from different semesters.
